A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the maintained discharge of rat ganglion cells is not simply a stochastic process, but is a complex mixture of stochastic and deterministic processes.

the maintained discharge of retinal ganglion neurons can be described by an integrate-andfire neuron model with a sinusoidal input, and the oscillation frequency is determined by the time constant of the neuron.

the maintained discharge of retinal ganglion is not random but is organized by oscillations in the frequency range 28-42 Hz, and that the oscillations in retinal ganglion discharge may be generated in the inner retina, perhaps by the amacrine cells, and are modulated by light.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the maintained discharge of rat RGCs is highly variable and can be characterized as a combination of a low frequency, low amplitude oscillation and high frequency, high amplitude oscillations that occur at a rate of approximately once every second.
the retina is not a static device, but is constantly generating oscillations that modulate the response of the ganglion cells.
the retina is not a passive device that simply transforms light into spike trains.
